title: THE CORNERS THAT HOLD TWO WALLS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made six frames for the far end, that is, the west end of the tabernacle, and two frames were made for the corners of the tabernacle at the far end. At these two corners the frames were double from the bottom all the way to the top and fitted into a single ring; both were made alike. So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases - two under each frame." - Exod 36:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The corner frames were different. Doubled from bottom to top, joined into a single ring, carrying the weight of two walls meeting at an angle.

Corners are stress points. That is where structures fail, and that is where God specified extra strength.

Some people occupy corner positions in life. The person who holds together two parts of a family that barely speak. The believer who is the only Christian in an office. The one who bridges generations in a church, or cultures in a community. That position carries strain from two directions at once.

If that is you, notice two things. First, God designed corners deliberately — you have not ended up there by accident. Second, He reinforced them. The corner frames were double.

Paul spoke of being pressed on every side but not crushed (2 Cor 4:8-9). Pressure is not the same as collapse when God supplies the strength.

And Scripture gives us the cornerstone Himself — Christ Jesus, in whom the whole building is joined together (Eph 2:20-21). Every corner in God's structure is held by Him.

If you are carrying weight from two directions today, He knows. He built you for that position and He will hold you in it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you in a "corner" position carrying pressure from two sides?
2. Where do you draw strength when pressed from multiple directions?
3. How does Christ as the cornerstone steady you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, where I feel pressure from every side, be my strength. Thank You that You are the cornerstone holding everything together. Amen.
